bound_context.question: What does the 75-byte leaf routine at 0x61bd4f0 do with (p, limit, uint32_t* value), and when does it return nullptr?

consumer_table.meaning: the nullptr contract is checked before the result is used

consumer_table.first_use: mov r12, rax, mov rcx, rax, ...
consumer_table.meaning: the advanced pointer is carried in another register
the advanced pointer is subtracted from a base to size a consumed range
never read inside the enclosing FDE (the call's only effect is the stored value)
rax is overwritten before being read

caller_census.contract: returns p+n (a pointer past the decoded varint) on success and nullptr on failure; the failure value is observable at the call site, since 27 of the 149 sites test it first
caller_census.method: every call target matching the window start is decoded with Capstone and attributed to the enclosing .eh_frame FDE; the instruction after the call is classified by how rax is first used

claim_anchors: semantics.tsv (24 anchors: claim -> target instruction address, bytes and decoded instruction)
environment_limits: the packet is static: the artifact is never executed and no source build is claimed
the emulator implements only the instructions this routine uses and raises on any other
the caller-side behaviour is read from the instruction after each call; it is not executed
ledger: cases.tsv (300 reviewable cases, 50 per family: the 1..5-byte varints plus the nullptr family) recording the limit, the outcome (ok/null), the decoded value and the next index; the boundary rows are kept verbatim and the full 2,400-case sweep is re-derived in memory by the tests

observations.text: the window 0x61bd4f0..0x61bd53b is one .eh_frame FDE and one leaf routine: no calls, no relocations, 27 instructions
p >= limit returns nullptr immediately and no byte is read (cmp %rsi,%rdi / jae 0x61bd538)
the continuation test is the sign bit of the byte just read (test %dil,%dil / js), so any byte >= 0x80 continues the varint
each continuation byte advances the shift by 7 and a shift above 28 is rejected, so at most four continuation bytes (five bytes in all) are accepted
after every continuation byte the advanced pointer is compared with limit and nullptr is returned if it reached it: a truncated varint is rejected, never answered with the bytes seen so far
the accumulator, the final shift and the store are 32-bit, so the decoded value is masked to 32 bits: 80 80 80 80 20 decodes to 0 and 80 80 80 80 7f to 0xf0000000
the successful return value is the pointer just past the last byte read (rax is advanced before the continuation test), not a count
the only memory accesses are one byte load per input byte and a single 32-bit store through value; a failed decode writes nothing
149 direct call sites in 45 caller FDEs; 27 of them test the returned pointer first (test rax,rax / je), so the nullptr contract is observable
the signature is const char* GetVarint32PtrFallback(const char* p, const char* limit, uint32_t* value): p in rdi, limit in rsi, value in rdx, read off the mangled name and the uses of rdi/rsi/rdx
the callers that test rax for zero are handling the decode failure ('no varint in range'), which is consistent with the nullptr return rather than with a count

unknowns: which call sites can actually reach the failure return at run time is not characterized (it depends on the buffer contents the callers are given)
the C++ types are inferred from the mangled signature and the shift widths; the packet does not prove them
the sibling windows in the same object (EncodeVarint32 0x61bd410, GetVarint64Ptr 0x61bd540) are separate windows and are not covered here
the body is byte-identical in 3 identical source objects; only 0x61bd4f0 is bound
the caller-side classification stops at the first use of rax; a value that is copied and then discarded is classified by its first use
